fields.paulfranklin\n\n 2016-05-31 21:50\n\ndev:
I think the problem is that people who make
changes like that tend to assume the whole
world is like their particular piece of the
world. Some linux systems (Arch I believe)
only have one Python, which is Python3, but
is called just "python" in their system.
(The gramps Windows AIO is like that IIRC.)
Other systems have both and differentiate by
calling one "python2" and "python3".

If I were offering an opinion, I'd say that
files like our setup.py shouldn't have a
shebang at the top at all. But that's not
the way somebody set it up. Whatever it is.
somebody will find it won't work for them.

I would imagine however that anybody trying
to run setup.py, like you, knows what to do
if they get a funny error, how to cope.

#!/usr/bin/env python

import sys
import os

if sys.version_info < (3, 2): # replace 2 by 8 to check for 3.8
f = os.popen('which python3')
python3 = f.read()
python = python3[:-1] + " --version"
new_command = python3[:-1]
for arg in sys.argv:
new_command += " " + arg
f = os.popen(python)
version = f.read().replace('Python ','').replace('.','')
if version > '320':
os.system(new_command)
os._exit(0)
else:
raise SystemExit("Gramps requires Python 3.2 or later.")
os._exit(255)
else:

continue. we have the good python version.
print("OK")
os._exit(0)
